title: Specific Heat Capacity — Units & Dimensional Formula
notes: Specific heat capacity c is the heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K. The defining relation is Q = mc Δθ, so c = Q / (m Δθ).
The SI unit is joule per kilogram per kelvin, J kg^-1 K^-1. A degree Celsius interval equals a kelvin interval, so J kg^-1 °C^-1 is the same size of unit.
Heat Q has the dimensions of energy, [M L^2 T^-2]. Mass is [M] and a temperature interval brings in [K]. Therefore [c] = [L^2 T^-2 K^-1].
Water's specific heat is about 4200 J kg^-1 K^-1, which is large. That is why a large mass of water changes temperature slowly for a given heat input.
The heat capacity of a whole body is C = mc, in J/K. Specific heat is a material property. Heat capacity belongs to one particular object.

Mixing problems use heat lost equals heat gained when the container is closed to outside heat. Each term is of the form mc Δθ, with the temperature change written as a positive quantity in that bookkeeping.
